subject: Estimating Items Parameters With Known Thetas

messages.author: 247c563800a43e5a
messages.subject: Estimating Items Parameters With Known Thetas
parts:
Hello,

For a given exam, I have a table with the response vector of each student (a vector of 0's and 1's indicating wrong/right answers) and their corresponding estimated latent trait. I do not have, however, the item parameters (a, b, c) of the 3PL model that computed those thetas in the first place. 

Is there any way to fit a model to compute the irt parameters for the items in that exam while using the thetas I already have (in other words, ensuring the resulting model generates thetas very similar to those that have been previously computed)?

Best,
Pedro

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Estimating Items Parameters With Known Thetas
parts:
Hi Pedro,

Unfortunately, no you won't be able to recover the most optimal item parameters given point estimates of the thetas, unfortunately, because the point estimates for each participant do not contain information pertaining to their complete sampling variability. Plus, each estimate has a certain degree of shrinkage/bias associated with the estimates, so even obtaining unbiased IRT parameter estimates is unlikely. This is the main problem with the JML estimation criteria too. See this thread.

Phil
